title: Come, Ye Disconsolate, Where'er Ye Languish
description: Come, Ye Disconsolate, Where'er Ye Languish in Tonic Solfa to HENLEY, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 575 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Invitation to the Mercy-seat”, where the book credits them to the Spiritual Songs.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HENLEY; any other Elevens and Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, ye dis-con-so-late, wher-e'er ye lan-guish; Come, at the mer-cy seat fer-vent-ly kneel: Here bring your woun-ded hearts, here tell your an-guish; Earth has no sor-row that heaven can-not heal.

lines: Come, ye disconsolate, where'er ye languish;
Come, at the mercy-seat fervently kneel:
Here bring your wounded hearts, here tell your anguish;
Earth has no sorrow that heaven cannot heal.
Joy of the desolate, light of the straying,
Hope of the penitent, fadeless and pure,
Here speaks the Comforter, tenderly saying,
Earth has no sorrow that heaven cannot cure.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to HENLEY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
